about.title: Emeryville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Emeryville is small — fewer than 12,000 residents tucked between Oakland and the Bay — but I-80 cuts right through it, and Powell Street, Hollis Street and 40th Street carry commuters and shoppers all day. In 2025, the city recorded 135 injury collisions and 3 traffic deaths. Behind that count are families whose lives changed in a moment. A wrongful death claim is how California lets those families seek accountability through the civil courts, separate from any criminal case the Alameda County District Attorney may or may not bring. The people who can file are limited by law: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The claim can cover funeral and burial expenses, the income and support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive does not handle the case itself. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who does, and who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Emeryville Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We know who has standing to file
items.desc: California limits who can bring a wrongful death claim — a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out who in your family qualifies before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock matters, and it varies
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, but the window is much shorter when a government entity — such as the agency responsible for a freeway or a city street — may be involved.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Our service is free, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. Your family should not have to weigh legal bills against grief.

items.question: If the crash happened on I-80 in Emeryville, is the deadline different?
items.answer: It can be. When a claim involves a public entity — for example, if road design or maintenance on a state freeway or a city-controlled street like Powell or Hollis is part of the picture — California requires a government claim to be filed far sooner than the usual two years. An attorney can evaluate quickly whether any public agency may share responsibility so no deadline is missed.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges in Alameda County. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate paths. A criminal case is brought by the District Attorney and is about punishment; it does not compensate your family for funeral costs, lost support, or the loss of companionship. A wrongful death claim is a civil action your family controls, and it can proceed whether or not charges are filed or result in a conviction.

items.question: What can a wrongful death claim actually cover?
items.answer: California law allows eligible family members to seek funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided over their lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship, guidance and care. Every family's situation is different, so no one can tell you in advance what a claim is worth. An independent attorney can explain what applies to your circumstances.
